item.title: Sparebar 0.1.7
item.description:
Keep a few spare batteries ready for your Codex allowance.
Available Codex usage resets now appear as a horizontal reserve beneath your allowance. Filled batteries stay on the left; confirmed resets used in Sparebar on this Mac stay on the right. Empty reserves say No spares available.
At 10% remaining or less, Use a spare offers an account and reset confirmation. Healthy allowance stays quiet. Sparebar never redeems automatically and always rechecks the provider result.
Interrupted requests keep the same request ID across retries and restarts, helping prevent accidental duplicate use. Reset support depends on your Codex CLI and account. Used history covers only confirmed resets in Sparebar on this Mac.
This is a preview release. Real redemption is left to the user's explicit action. Launch at login after a real login, physical sleep/wake, VoiceOver, and sustained battery use still need manual verification.

item.title: Sparebar 0.1.6
item.description:
Your little battery drains again, and its numbers keep up.
The robot's battery fill follows the displayed allowance during normal service. The eyes stay readable across both filled and empty areas. During service problems or unconfirmed status, the face stays full so the health signal remains clear.
Automatic allowance checks now recover if their timer falls behind, so an old reading does not stay unavailable until you refresh manually. Retry limits still apply when a provider cannot be reached.
The normal eyes have equal widths on Retina displays, with a slightly clearer gap between them. Battery changes respect Reduce Motion.
This is a preview release. Launch at login after a real login, physical sleep/wake, VoiceOver, and sustained battery use still need manual verification.

item.title: Sparebar 0.1.5
item.description:
Your robot keeps an eye on the services you actually use.
Choose which services affect the eyes and status panel in Settings > Service health. OpenAI and Claude each have a compact Choose button with their own service list.
ChatGPT, Codex, claude.ai, and Claude Code start enabled. APIs, developer consoles, government services, Claude Cowork, and Ads Platform start off. Your choices are saved separately for each provider.
Unselected services no longer trigger incident eyes or reminders. Clear a provider's choices to stop its service checks; allowance readings continue independently. Changing your selection does not pretend an incident recovered.
Checks still run about every five minutes while awake. If a report does not identify affected services clearly, Sparebar shows the status as unconfirmed.

item.title: Sparebar 0.1.4
item.description:
Your robot now keeps an eye on service outages.
Sparebar checks official OpenAI and Claude status pages about every five minutes while your Mac is awake, for the tools you have enabled.
The robot's eyes tell the story: squares mean no incidents reported, thin lines mean degraded service, crosses mean an outage, and muted lines mean status is unconfirmed. Open the panel to see affected services and their official status pages. The percentage still shows your allowance.
A gentle blink marks a new incident. Outage reminders stop after you open the panel, and happy eyes briefly celebrate recovery. Reduce Motion keeps the eyes still.
Find the eye-shape guide and polling details in Settings under Service health. No extra account, API key, or model calls are needed.

item.title: Sparebar 0.1.3
item.description:
Sparebar keeps itself fresh - one less thing to remember.
New versions download in the background and install when you quit. Sparebar never restarts on its own.
A small orange dot lets you know an update is available. Open Sparebar to see what's new and choose Update and Restart whenever it suits you.
Prefer to choose each download? Turn off Automatic updates in Settings. Sparebar will still check once a day and let you know when something new is ready.
